text:
Maya (CS): Nebula Health escalated — after our Dedicated quantization rollout last Wed their search rerank precision for clinical queries dropped ~12%. They provided before/after examples and are asking for ETA on a fix.

Ethan (Product PM): Ack, thanks Maya. Can you paste a couple of the customer examples inline? Also: did they pin a model version or are they on the latest hosted alias?

Maya (CS): Pasted below. They say they were pinned to `rnwd-embed-v2.1-q8` on Dedicated pool A.

Maya (CS): ````
query: "best treatment for stage II hypertension in elderly"
before_top1: "...guidelines recommend lifestyle first, then ACE inhibitors..."
after_top1: "...try herbal supplements, consult forum..."
````

Priya (ML Eng): :eyes: That looks like semantic drift, lower embedding fidelity on medical phrasing. Quick checks: 1) full-batch cosine histograms, 2) any recent quantization kernel change, 3) index sharding differences. I'll run internal eval w/ their sample set.

Riley (SRE): DevOps Bot created ticket INF-5892 for Nebula escalations. Link: https://redwood/incidents/INF-5892 :white_check_mark:

DevOps Bot: Ticket INF-5892 created by Maya (CS) — severity: P2, owner: unassigned.

Sam (Sales): Customer is asking for a timeline to tell their CTO. They tagged this as blocking a feature launch. If Product needs extra-priority, we should call it out now.

Ethan (Product PM): This needs product triage. Two paths: 1) short-term mitigation: roll back quantization on Dedicated for Nebula or switch them to `rnwd-embed-v2.1-fp16` variant + reindex; 2) longer-term: investigate quantization calibration and add eval gating for medical domains. Which does Support prefer?

Maya (CS): Customer prefers a fast fix — reindex or rollback — they can tolerate a short maintenance window.

Priya (ML Eng): I'll run a quick ablation tonight comparing v2.1-fp16 vs v2.1-q8 on their sample of 2.3k medical queries. If fp16 regains >10% MAP, rollback is best short-term. Also propose a lightweight recalibration script: `scripts/calibrate_quant.py --dataset nebula_sample.json --target-threshold 0.95`

Ethan (Product PM): OK. For roadmap/prioritization: propose we add a scoped initiative "quantized-embed-safety-net" with acceptance criteria: (a) automated domain-sensitive eval on deploy, (b) canary rollback toggle at customer/pool level, (c) documented perf delta matrix for top 5 customers. Scope estimate: 2 sprints to deliver canary + rollback UX + simple gated eval; 4 sprints for calibration tooling and autorollback. Thoughts?

Sam (Sales): Sounds reasonable. CTO wants a committed date — can we promise a rollback within 24-48 hours for Nebula if Priya's test shows regression?

Priya (ML Eng): If tests show regression tonight, we can push an emergency rollback to their Dedicated pool within 24 hours assuming maintenance window approved. Reindexing will take longer depending on index size (estimate 3-6 hours).

Ethan (Product PM): Decision for triage call: immediate short-term action = allow CS to schedule rollback for Nebula to `fp16` if Priya confirms metric regain. Product will scope and prioritize the initiative at next planning; I'll slot it as a high-severity backlog item and request 1 engineer for an initial spike.

Maya (CS): I'll inform Nebula: we'll run analysis tonight and may ask to schedule a rollback maintenance window tomorrow.

Riley (SRE): Please attach a short repro and the sample IDs to the INF-5892 ticket. Also include topk logs + cosine distribution snapshot: ````
cosine_hist_before = [0.92,0.88,0.81,0.75,...]
cosine_hist_after  = [0.78,0.70,0.62,0.58,...]
````

Maya (CS): Added samples and logs to INF-5892. Noted customer urgency.

Ethan (Product PM): I'll create the backlog item PROD-3142 with the spike and acceptance criteria. Owner: unassigned -> assigning to Priya for spike.

Priya (ML Eng): I'll own the spike. Plan: run eval tonight, post results in INF-5892, and recommend rollback if MAP delta >8%.

Sam (Sales): Thanks team — I'll relay to Nebula and ask for a maintenance window.

Maya (CS): :thumbsup: Closing loop for now, will post updates later today.
